subject: Plotting the difference (y1 - y2) at each timepoint

messages.author: 295be70ee92d8341
messages.subject: Plotting the difference (y1 - y2) at each timepoint
parts:
I have some data in the form:

Time, Strain, Value
0, A, 56
30, A, 43
60, A, 12
0, B, 11
30, B, 14
60, B, 6

The results from strain B are just baseline, so I want to subtract them from the stain A values at each time-point and just plot the difference. Is there any way I can specify this in 'aes'? Obviously I could copy the whole thing into excel but I will need to do this many, many times so if there is a simple trick either in ggplot2 or R more generally then it would be very helpful!

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Re: Plotting the difference (y1 - y2) at each timepoint
parts: I don't think there is a way to do it in `aes` directly, though a couple options you could do are 1) `ddply` in the `plyr` package, grouping by "Time" and doing the subtraction in each subset or 2) `reshape2` package's `cast` function. That will make the data wide and allow you to subtract. Then you can use `melt` to get it back into long form, which `ggplot2` likes.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Plotting the difference (y1 - y2) at each timepoint
parts:
Here's what Brandon is talking about. Note that I had to remove the
spaces between values in your data because R was reading Strain as a
factor with levels " A" and " B" (note the leading space). That
behavior may be a dplyr artefact, but I don't know for sure.

The following code worked for me:

DF <- read.table(header = TRUE, text = "
Time,Strain,Value
0,A,56
30,A,43
60,A,12
0,B,11
30,B,14
60,B,6", sep = ",")

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

DF %>% spread(Strain, Value) %>%
mutate(Diff = A - B) %>%
ggplot(aes(x = Time, y = Diff)) +
geom_point()



# It's instructive to define

(d <- DF %>% spread(Strain, Value) %>%
mutate(Diff = A - B))

to see what spread() and mutate() are doing. The spread() function
behaves similarly to reshape2::dcast(), as Brandon noted. The levels
of Strain become the new variable names in the output data set, much
like dcast(). From there, the definition of Diff within mutate() is
straightforward and the result data frame is input as the first [data]
argument of ggplot().

Dennis
